soja.name: Soybean
soja.sowing_window: November to December (first crop); December after a winter cereal (second crop).
soja.rotation.notes: Repeating it increases late-season diseases and stink bugs; it shares pathogens with peanut.
soja.agronomic_notes: It fixes nitrogen, but exports a lot in the grain: the net N balance is close to zero. It leaves little residue that breaks down quickly, so the wind-erosion risk is high. The critical period is grain filling (R3-R6).
sources: FAO-56 (Allen et al., 1998), Table 12: crop coefficients Kc

maiz.name: Corn
maiz.sowing_window: Early: September to October. Late: December (more common in rainfed fields, to avoid drought at flowering).
maiz.rotation.notes: Repeating it increases pests (fall armyworm, stem borer) and the corn leafhopper that spreads corn stunt.
maiz.agronomic_notes: It uses the most water in the catalog and is very sensitive to drought at flowering. It leaves a lot of residue: it protects the soil and adds carbon. Its rainfed yield in San Luis depends heavily on water stored at planting.
sources: FAO-56 (Allen et al., 1998), Table 12: crop coefficients Kc

trigo.name: Wheat
trigo.rotation.notes: It shares diseases with barley; avoid wheat after wheat.
trigo.agronomic_notes: San Luis gets little rain in winter: rainfed wheat depends on water stored in the soil profile, so its relative yield is low. Sensitive to heat waves during grain filling. It allows second-crop soybean if water is left over.

cebada.name: Barley
cebada.sowing_window: May to July; somewhat shorter than wheat.
cebada.agronomic_notes: Shorter cycle than wheat: it frees the plot earlier for a second crop. Malting barley usually needs a contract with maltsters, which are not in San Luis.

sorgo.name: Sorghum
sorgo.sowing_window: October to December, with warm soil.
sorgo.rotation.notes: It shares pests with corn (aphids, stem borer).
sorgo.agronomic_notes: More drought- and heat-tolerant than corn: it can pause growth and resume with rain. It leaves a lot of residue. Widely used for silage and grazing in mixed farms in San Luis.

girasol.name: Sunflower
girasol.rotation.notes: Sclerotinia and Verticillium wilt mean it should not be repeated within 3 or 4 years; rapeseed shares Sclerotinia.
girasol.agronomic_notes: Deep roots: it uses water from deep layers and tolerates drought. It leaves little residue: high erosion risk. Birds cause damage.

mani.name: Peanut
mani.sowing_window: October to November; includes lifting and drying in the field.
mani.rotation.notes: Peanut smut requires long rotations; it shares pathogens with soybean.
mani.agronomic_notes: It suits the sandy soils of eastern San Luis. Lifting leaves the soil very loose and bare: it is the crop with the highest wind-erosion risk. It is usually sold under contract to processing plants.

alfalfa.name: Alfalfa
alfalfa.rotation.notes: Autotoxicity: do not reseed alfalfa after alfalfa without several years in between.
alfalfa.agronomic_notes: Very deep roots: it uses water from layers other crops cannot reach, but it uses a lot over the year. It fixes nitrogen and improves soil structure. The basis of mixed crop-livestock systems.

pastura_perenne.name: Perennial pasture
pastura_perenne.sowing_window: Autumn for mixes with alfalfa; spring-summer for warm-season grasses (weeping lovegrass, digitaria).
pastura_perenne.rotation.notes: When the pasture is broken up, a summer cereal is best to use the released nitrogen.
pastura_perenne.agronomic_notes: Warm-season grasses (weeping lovegrass, digitaria) are central to livestock farming in semi-arid San Luis: they cover the soil year-round and rebuild organic matter. If the mix includes alfalfa or another legume, it also adds nitrogen (not counted by default).
sources: FAO-56 (Allen et al., 1998), Table 12: crop coefficients Kc

agua-riego.name: Sorghum – wheat with supplemental irrigation
agua-riego.rationale: With irrigation, it replaces corn with sorghum (lower demand) and uses a winter cereal that consumes water when ET0 is lowest, to cut irrigation volume.
management: adjust the irrigation depth to sorghum, which needs less water than corn

agua-semiarido.name: Sorghum – sunflower – millet with long fallows
agua-semiarido.rationale: It uses the catalog's most drought-tolerant summer crops, one with a very short cycle, and leaves long fallows to store water in the soil profile.
management: control weeds during the fallow so they don't use the stored water

agua-subhumedo.name: Sorghum – sunflower – soybean
agua-subhumedo.rationale: It replaces corn with sorghum and adds sunflower (deep roots) to lower water demand while still producing grain.
management: control weeds during the fallows so they don't use the stored water

suelo-semiarido.name: Perennial pasture (3 years) – cover crop – sorghum
suelo-semiarido.rationale: Crop-livestock rotation: the perennial pasture covers the soil year-round and rebuilds organic matter; when it is broken up, sorghum uses the released nitrogen.
management: own livestock or forage sales so the pasture generates income
terminate the cover crop in time (August-September) so the soil profile recharges before the summer crop

suelo-general.name: Cover crop – soybean – vetch – corn
suelo-general.rationale: It covers the soil in both winters: the grass before soybean (stops erosion) and the legume before corn (adds nitrogen).
management: terminate the cover crop in time (August-September) so the soil profile recharges before the summer crop
obtain cover-crop seed and budget for planting and termination costs

div-semiarido.name: Sorghum – oats – sunflower – vetch – millet
div-semiarido.rationale: Five crops from three families, with short, drought-tolerant cycles; the oat green forage brings in livestock.
management: plan five different crops (planting, inputs and machinery)

div-general.name: Soybean – wheat – vetch – sunflower – corn
div-general.rationale: Five crops from three families, alternating summer and winter; it keeps sunflower 4 years apart and precedes corn with a deep-rooted crop.
management: plan a four-year sequence
terminate the cover crop in time (August-September) so the soil profile recharges before the summer crop

rent-riego.name: Corn – peanut – wheat/second-crop soybean
rent-riego.rationale: With irrigation, it prioritizes the crops with the highest relative income and includes a wheat/soybean double crop.
management: secure a sales contract for the peanut
plant the second-crop soybean as soon as the wheat is harvested

rent-semiarido.name: Peanut – late corn – sunflower
rent-semiarido.rationale: It prioritizes high relative-income crops adapted to sandy soils (peanut) and plants corn late to avoid drought at flowering.
management: secure a sales contract for the peanut
cover the soil after peanut lifting, which leaves it very exposed to erosion

rent-subhumedo.name: Soybean – wheat/second-crop soybean – corn
rent-subhumedo.rationale: A high-income cropping sequence with a wheat/soybean double crop.
management: check soil-profile water at wheat planting: the double crop only pays off if water is stored

mixta-sa-1.name: Sorghum – vetch – sunflower – soybean
mixta-sa-1.rationale: It combines a drought-tolerant crop, a short legume cover and a deep-rooted crop.
management: terminate the cover crop in time (August-September) so the soil profile recharges before the summer crop

mixta-sa-2.name: Cover crop – sunflower – vetch – sorghum – millet
mixta-sa-2.rationale: Cover in both winters with drought-tolerant summer crops.
management: terminate the cover crop in time (August-September) so the soil profile recharges before the summer crop
obtain cover-crop seed and budget for planting and termination costs

mixta-sa-3.name: Oat green forage – sorghum – sunflower – soybean
mixta-sa-3.rationale: It brings in livestock with a winter green forage and two drought-tolerant summer crops.
management: have livestock to make use of the green forage

mixta-sh-1.name: Cover crop – soybean – vetch – sorghum
mixta-sh-1.rationale: Short winter cover crops and sorghum instead of corn to lower water demand.
management: terminate the cover crop in time (August-September) so the soil profile recharges before the summer crop
obtain cover-crop seed and budget for planting and termination costs

mixta-sh-2.name: Wheat/second-crop soybean – vetch – corn
mixta-sh-2.rationale: A double crop for income and a legume before corn to add nitrogen.
management: terminate the cover crop in time (August-September) so the soil profile recharges before the summer crop
check soil-profile water at wheat planting: the double crop only pays off if water is stored

mixta-sh-3.name: Soybean – cover crop – sunflower – vetch – corn
mixta-sh-3.rationale: Three cash crops from three families with cover in two of the three winters.
management: terminate the cover crop in time (August-September) so the soil profile recharges before the summer crop
